chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave, and he bore her children. Then he divorced her, and she did not stay with her children, but married another man. When the slave heard that she had married, he wanted to take his children from her, saying, 'I am more entitled to them than you, since you have married.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'It is not for the slave to take her children from her, and if she marries, she is more entitled to her children than he is as long as he remains a slave. When he is freed, then he is more entitled to them than she is.'
ai.seo_question: Who has custody of children from a free woman and a slave after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *al-ahrabb al-walad* (the one with greater freedom has priority in custody) within Shia jurisprudence, highlighting how social status influences parental rights. It clarifies that the slave husband's right is suspended during his servitude, allowing the free mother to retain custody even after remarriage, until his manumission restores his superior claim. This ruling underscores the interplay between *‘ubudiyyah* (slavery) and *hurriyyah* (freedom) in determining familial authority.
